Oblique Spaceships in Rule-Sequence Cellular Automata

About this archive CA notation and normalization TXT list

These cellular automata run on a two-dimensional square grid, where each cell interacts with its eight surrounding neighbors. Rules are numbered 1, 2, ..., and a repeating rule sequence specifies which rule updates the entire grid at each generation. All cells update simultaneously using the selected rule.

For example, Seq 122 applies Rule 1, then Rule 2 twice, and repeats. Cells can have two or more states, and different rules can use different state counts.

Seq 1 repeats a single rule; Seq 12 alternates two rules; Seq 122 repeats a three-generation sequence.

This repository collects oblique spaceships found in these systems: patterns that repeat while shifting in a direction that is neither horizontal, vertical nor diagonal. Each entry provides its rules, sequence, initial pattern and a runnable browser demo.

This complete list records oblique spaceships discovered by Kazuhiro Tanimoto in this study. It includes many that require specific initial structures, including examples extremely unlikely to emerge from random initial configurations. Many entries are related variants, and the collection has not yet been fully organized.

4,798 entries · Snapshot 2026-10-12. Click a rule set to run its recorded structure. Click No, slope or Report date to sort the list.

Reading a record

B/S/C gives birth and survival neighbor counts and the state count. Only state-1 neighbors are counted. Seq gives the repeated temporal program; Init gives the initial pattern. The demo URL includes the complete expression.

For a single-rule cellular automaton, define one rule and use Seq 1 to apply it every generation.

(dx,dy)c/p records the full displacement after p generations. The demo shows upper-right motion, with positive y upwards. The velocity fraction is not reduced. Population counts all nonzero states. Slope is dx/dy.
